regions.label: Dentate gyrus
regions.sub: GC, MC, HIPP, PV+ BC, AAC

cells.label: Granule cell
cells.dend: molecular layer (IML, MML, OML), cone-shaped, spiny
cells.axon: mossy fiber: collaterals in the hilus, then stratum lucidum of CA3 with giant boutons
cells.about: The principal cell of the dentate. Very sparse firing; reads the perforant path on its spines and passes a sparse code to CA3 through some of the largest synapses in the brain.

phys.text: Sparse: in a given place most granule cells are silent; active ones fire at low rates.
The spike starts in the axon 20-30 um from the soma and runs down the mossy fibre at about 0.24 m/s.

lab.text: PTEN loss in granule cells makes them hypertrophic, with ectopic somata, hilar basal dendrites and mossy fibres sprouting into the inner molecular layer, and is enough to cause epilepsy.

cells.line: The dentate's principal cell: sparse firing, giant mossy-fibre synapses onto CA3.

cells.label: Semilunar granule cell
cells.dend: wide, half-moon fan through the molecular layer
cells.axon: like a GC: hilus and CA3, plus IML collaterals
cells.about: A granule-cell relative with its soma out in the inner molecular layer and a broad dendritic fan. Persistent firing after perforant-path input; drives hilar cells.

phys.text: Fire persistently for seconds after a perforant-path input, unlike granule cells.

cells.line: A granule-cell relative with its soma out in the inner molecular layer.

cells.label: Mossy cell
cells.dend: thick, mostly in the hilus, covered proximally in thorny excrescences (where mossy-fiber boutons land)
cells.axon: to the inner molecular layer, mostly at other septotemporal levels and the other side (associational/commissural)
cells.about: The excitatory cell of the hilus. Takes mossy-fiber input on its thorns and feeds it back to granule cells (and interneurons) far along the hippocampus, landing on the proximal dendrites in the IML.

phys.text: Much more active than granule cells, with several place fields each.

cells.line: The hilus's excitatory cell: takes mossy fibres, feeds granule cells far away.

cells.label: HIPP cell
cells.axon: outer two-thirds of the molecular layer, where the perforant path lands
cells.about: Hilar Perforant-Path-associated interneuron. Inhibits granule-cell distal dendrites right where the entorhinal input arrives: feedback inhibition of the perforant-path synapse.

phys.text: A regular-spiking (non-fast-spiking) SST+ cell that inhibits the distal dendrites.

lab.text: A Kcnt1 gain-of-function variant makes non-fast-spiking GABAergic neurons less excitable (cortex).

cells.line: SST+ interneuron of the hilus; inhibits where the perforant path lands.

cells.label: PV+ basket cell
cells.dend: up through the molecular layer and down into the hilus
cells.axon: basket of terminals around granule-cell somata in the GCL
cells.about: Perisomatic inhibition: wraps granule-cell bodies in terminals. Fed forward by the perforant path and back by granule cells; sets the timing of granule-cell output.

phys.text: Fast-spiking: hundreds of spikes a second without slowing; paces gamma and times granule-cell output.

cells.line: PV+ basket cell: perisomatic inhibition of granule cells.

cells.label: Axo-axonic cell
cells.axon: cartridges on granule-cell axon initial segments at the GCL-hilus border
cells.about: Chandelier cell. Its terminals line up on the axon initial segments of granule cells: the last word on whether a granule cell fires.

phys.text: Fast-spiking PV+ cell whose synapses sit on the axon initial segment.

cells.line: Chandelier cell: inhibition on the axon initial segment.

cells.label: MEC stellate cell
cells.dend: several primary dendrites spreading in layers I-II
cells.axon: medial perforant path: middle molecular layer of the DG, and CA3 slm
cells.about: Grid-cell territory. Layer II stellate cells of the medial entorhinal cortex give the medial perforant path, which lands on the middle third of the dentate molecular layer.

phys.text: Many are grid cells; theta-frequency membrane oscillations in vitro.

lab.text: A synchronous MEC layer II volley onto the middle molecular layer is DS2.

cells.line: MEC layer II stellate cell: the medial perforant path (DS2).

cells.label: LEC fan cell
cells.dend: fan of dendrites up into layer I, little basal tree
cells.axon: lateral perforant path: outer molecular layer of the DG, and CA3 slm
cells.about: The object/context side of the entorhinal cortex. Layer IIa fan cells of the lateral entorhinal cortex give the lateral perforant path, which lands on the outer third of the molecular layer.

phys.text: Lateral entorhinal cells signal objects, odors and elapsed time.

lab.text: A synchronous LEC layer II volley onto the outer molecular layer is DS1.

cells.line: LEC layer II cell: the lateral perforant path (DS1).

cells.label: CA3 pyramidal cell
cells.dend: basal in oriens, apical through lucidum (mossy-fiber thorns), radiatum and lacunosum-moleculare
cells.axon: recurrent collaterals in CA3, Schaffer collaterals to CA1 radiatum/oriens, commissural to the other side; some back to the hilus
cells.about: The recurrent network. Takes mossy fibers proximally, its own collaterals in the middle, and entorhinal input distally; sends Schaffer collaterals to CA1.

phys.text: Burst-firing place cells; CA3 population bursts start sharp-wave ripples.

cells.line: CA3 pyramidal cell: mossy-fibre input, recurrent network, Schaffer output.

cells.label: CA1 pyramidal cell
cells.dend: basal in oriens, apical through radiatum (Schaffer input) to a tuft in lacunosum-moleculare (EC layer III input)
cells.axon: through the alveus to the subiculum and deep entorhinal cortex
cells.about: The main output of the hippocampus proper. Compares CA3 input in radiatum with direct entorhinal input in lacunosum-moleculare.

phys.text: Place cells that shift their spikes earlier in each theta cycle as an animal crosses the field (phase precession).
Fire together during sharp-wave ripples, replaying recent paths.

cells.line: CA1 pyramidal cell: the main output of the hippocampus proper.

cells.label: O-LM cell
cells.axon: up across the layers to lacunosum-moleculare
cells.about: Oriens-lacunosum moleculare cell. Driven by CA1 pyramidal cells, inhibits their distal tufts where the entorhinal input lands: the CA1 counterpart of the HIPP cell.

phys.text: Fire at the trough of CA1 theta and fall silent during ripples.

lab.text: SST+ cells are among the non-fast-spiking interneurons a Kcnt1 gain-of-function variant makes less excitable.

cells.line: SST+ O-LM interneuron: inhibits CA1 tufts in lacunosum-moleculare.

connections.label: lateral perforant path
connections.about: LEC layer II to the outer third of the molecular layer, on granule-cell distal dendrites. The current sink of DS1.

connections.label: medial perforant path
connections.about: MEC layer II to the middle third of the molecular layer. The current sink of DS2.

connections.label: mossy fibers
connections.about: Granule-cell axons to CA3 stratum lucidum: giant, detonator-like boutons on the thorns of CA3 pyramidal cells.

connections.label: mossy-fiber collaterals
connections.about: On the way to CA3, mossy fibers branch in the hilus and land on mossy-cell thorny excrescences.

connections.label: mossy fibers to hilar interneurons
connections.about: Most mossy-fiber synapses are on interneurons (small en-passant boutons and filopodia), not on mossy cells or CA3.

connections.label: associational/commissural
connections.about: Mossy-cell axons to the inner molecular layer: granule-cell proximal dendrites, mostly at other levels and on the other side.

connections.label: HIPP to distal dendrites
connections.about: SST+ HIPP axons inhibit granule-cell distal dendrites in the outer two-thirds, in register with the perforant path.

connections.label: semilunar granule cells to hilar cells

pathways.label: Trisynaptic loop
pathways.blurb: The classic route from entorhinal cortex through all three hippocampal stages and back out.

hops.say: MEC layer II stellate cells fire.
The medial perforant path crosses the hippocampal fissure and lands on the middle third of the dentate molecular layer.
A few granule cells reach threshold: the dentate is a sparse, pattern-separating gate.
Mossy fibers run through the hilus into CA3 stratum lucidum: one giant bouton can fire a CA3 cell.
CA3 pyramidal cells; their recurrent collaterals let the network complete a pattern.
Schaffer collaterals arc through CA1 stratum radiatum and oriens.
CA1 pyramidal cells compare it with direct entorhinal input on their tufts.
CA1 axons leave through the alveus to the subiculum ...
... and the loop closes in deep layers of the entorhinal cortex.
Deep EC sends the result back to the neocortex.

pathways.label: Lateral perforant path
pathways.blurb: LEC fan cells to the outer molecular layer. Its population volley is DS1.

hops.say: Perirhinal cortex (objects, odors) drives the lateral entorhinal cortex.
Layer IIa fan cells of LEC fire.
Their axons land on the outer third of the molecular layer, on the farthest reach of granule-cell dendrites.
Granule cells and the interneurons whose dendrites reach OML are depolarized there.
HIPP cells inhibit the very same stretch of dendrite.

pathways.label: Medial perforant path
pathways.blurb: MEC stellate cells to the middle molecular layer. Its population volley is DS2.

hops.say: Postrhinal cortex (space, scenes) drives the medial entorhinal cortex.
Layer II stellate (grid) cells of MEC fire.
Their axons land on the middle third of the molecular layer.
The same fibers excite basket cells: feed-forward inhibition.
Basket cells clamp granule-cell somata a few milliseconds later.

pathways.label: Temporoammonic path
pathways.blurb: EC layer III straight to CA1, skipping the dentate and CA3.

hops.say: EC layer III pyramidal cells.
Axons run to CA1 stratum lacunosum-moleculare, on the distal tufts.
CA1 pyramidal cells get the direct cortical view next to the CA3 view in radiatum.
O-LM cells inhibit the same tufts: CA1 can gate its own entorhinal input.

pathways.label: Mossy-cell loop
pathways.blurb: Granule cells excite mossy cells, which excite granule cells far away.

hops.say: Granule cells fire.
Mossy-fiber collaterals in the hilus hit mossy-cell thorny excrescences.
Mossy cells fire (they are much more active than granule cells).
Their axons end in the inner molecular layer, mostly at other levels and on the other side.
They also excite interneurons: net effect on granule cells can be inhibition.

pathways.label: Dentate inhibition
pathways.blurb: Three interneurons, three places on a granule cell.

hops.say: HIPP: distal dendrites, with the perforant path.
PV+ basket cells: the soma.
Axo-axonic cells: the axon initial segment, the last word.

pathways.label: CA2 loop
pathways.blurb: A disynaptic route from EC layer II through CA2 to CA1.

hops.say: EC layer II axons excite CA2 pyramidal cells strongly.
CA2: social memory.
CA2 axons end in CA1 stratum oriens (and radiatum).

pathways.label: Back-projection
pathways.blurb: CA3 talks back to the dentate.

hops.say: CA3 pyramidal cells, especially CA3c near the hilus.
Collaterals return to the hilus and contact mossy cells and interneurons.
Mossy cells pass it to granule-cell proximal dendrites.

pathways.label: Hippocampal output
pathways.blurb: Where the hippocampus sends its answer.

hops.say: CA1 pyramidal cells.
To the subiculum.
To the pre- and parasubiculum.
Through the fimbria-fornix to the mammillary bodies, septum and nucleus accumbens.
And back to deep entorhinal cortex.

ds.label: DS1
ds.say: LEC layer II fires together. The lateral perforant path depolarizes the outer third of the molecular layer in both blades: a current sink in OML, with the return current (source) nearer the granule cells. Hilar interneurons burst.

ds.label: DS2
ds.say: MEC layer II fires together. The medial perforant path depolarizes the middle third: a current sink in MML, flanked by sources. DS2 is usually the larger of the two. Hilar interneurons burst.

probe.label: Linear probe
probe.note: Placement only; no recording is attached.

region_lines.DG: Dentate gyrus: the input stage, where the perforant path lands and dentate spikes happen.
region_lines.CA3: CA3: the recurrent network; mossy fibres in, Schaffer collaterals out.
region_lines.CA2: CA2: a small field with strong entorhinal input; social memory.
region_lines.CA1: CA1: compares CA3 and entorhinal input; the main output of the hippocampus proper.
region_lines.SUB: Subiculum: the output of the hippocampal formation.
region_lines.ENTl: Lateral entorhinal cortex: objects, odors, time; the lateral perforant path (DS1).
region_lines.ENTm: Medial entorhinal cortex: grid cells; the medial perforant path (DS2).
region_lines.PERI: Perirhinal cortex: objects; drives the lateral entorhinal cortex.
region_lines.VISpor: Postrhinal cortex (VISpor): scenes and space; drives the medial entorhinal cortex.

crowd.note: One dot per cell. Granule cells: the stereological count for C57BL/6 (Kempermann et al. 1997) spread through this atlas's granule layer. Other densities are assumed from soma size and packing.

lamina.label: OML1
lamina.name: outer molecular layer, upper (suprapyramidal) blade
lamina.line: Lateral perforant path (LEC II) ends here; the DS1 sink.
lamina.how: derived: proportional depth (thirds) inside an Allen structure

lamina.label: MML1
lamina.name: middle molecular layer, upper blade
lamina.line: Medial perforant path (MEC II) ends here; the DS2 sink.
lamina.how: derived: proportional depth (thirds) inside an Allen structure

lamina.label: IML1
lamina.name: inner molecular layer, upper blade
lamina.line: Mossy-cell (associational/commissural) input on proximal dendrites.
lamina.how: derived: proportional depth (thirds) inside an Allen structure

lamina.label: GCL1
lamina.name: granule cell layer, upper blade
lamina.line: Granule-cell bodies, packed; basket and chandelier cells at its edge.

lamina.label: MML2

lamina.how: derived: proportional depth (thirds) inside an Allen structure

lamina.label: OML2

lamina.label: CA1 so
lamina.name: stratum oriens

lamina.name: stratum pyramidale

lamina.name: stratum pyramidale

lamina.how: derived: Nissl-dense sheet inside the Allen CA field

lamina.label: CA2 sr
lamina.name: stratum radiatum
lamina.line: Apical dendrites: Schaffer (CA1) or recurrent (CA3) input; the sharp-wave sink in CA1.
lamina.how: derived: proportional depth (thirds) inside an Allen structure

lamina.label: CA2 slm
lamina.name: stratum lacunosum-moleculare
lamina.line: Distal tufts: entorhinal input; theta is largest near here.
lamina.how: derived: proportional depth (thirds) inside an Allen structure

lamina.name: stratum oriens
